Subject: Production: live stream sessions going silent (ongoing since 14:50 PST)

Hi Vanessa / Marissa —

We're seeing recurring incidents in production where our clients maintain an open WebSocket to Redwood, the initial tokens stream fine for a few seconds, then the socket remains open but no data (no chunked frames) are received for 30-90s. When the stream resumes, it often returns a burst of tokens, or the client sees an error. This started ~14:50 PST and has affected ~12% of sessions for one of our busiest routes (realtime.chat).

Impact metrics we observe on our side: p50 increase ~220ms -> 1.1s, p95 spikes to 6.8s, error rate up from 0.3% to 3.4% for that route, sustained throughput drop ~18%.

Attached a short client capture and streaming stats (client_capture_20270318.txt, streaming-stats-20270318.csv).

Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing anything on your side for connections tied to BrightLeaf's dedicated pool (customer id BL-3201)? We need an expedited root cause and mitigation; this is customer-impacting during their business hours.

Thanks,
Alex
Customer Success / BrightLeaf AI

Quick findings from a first-pass triage (logs attached: proxy_heap_dump_20270318.tar.gz):

- Observed pattern: edge proxy (nginx-based) backlog rising for connections originating from BrightLeaf's dedicated pool. Queue depth and write buffer latency spike correlate with client-visible silence windows.
- Metric highlights (15:40-16:30 PST): proxy_write_queue.p95 -> 420ms to 2.8s; proxy_worker_temp_stall events: 0 -> 24 in 40m on pool-gray-7 (hosts serving BL-3201).
- Heap traces show many idle goroutines waiting on socket write completions; kernel-level write buffers appear to be forced into blocking due to upstream worker stalls (suspect: KV cache compaction triggered by burst).
- Hypothesis: a combination of (1) write buffer backpressure in the proxy, (2) delayed ack processing from the downstream runtime, and (3) heartbeat/keepalive timeouts with the client side delaying chunk flush until the buffers drain. This manifests as open sockets with no chunks for extended periods.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (recommended order):
1) Increase proxy socket write buffer timeout and lower proxy output buffer high-water mark (quick config tweak) — low risk, immediate.
2) Roll a hotfix to runtime that short-circuits chunk ack handling (force periodic flush every 250ms) — medium risk, requires quick QA.
3) If necessary, perform rolling restart of pool-gray-7 edge nodes (require exec sign-off for customer-dedicated nodes).

Dev/Vanessa: I can implement (1) in the next 20 minutes and push a canary to 10% of BL-3201 sessions. I have attached a short extraction of the proxy heap and a CSV of the streaming metrics we pulled.

Markus
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
